title: Profiling & Debugging Performance
description: Use Vue Devtools and browser tools to find and fix bottlenecks.

slides.title: Vue Devtools Performance Tab
slides.content:
# Inspecting Component Render Times

The Vue Devtools extension includes a **Performance** tab. It records component rendering times and shows a flame graph.

1. Click the **Record** button.
2. Interact with your app.
3. Stop recording to see which components took the most time to render.

This helps you identify slow components and optimize them.

slides.title: Browser DevTools Performance
slides.content:
# Chrome/Edge Performance Panel

The browser's Performance tab gives a low‑level view of JavaScript execution, layout, and painting.

- Record a performance profile.
- Look for long tasks, layout thrashing, or unnecessary reflows.
- Identify expensive functions (including Vue's reactivity).

slides.title: Common Bottlenecks to Look For
slides.content:
# What to Optimize

- **Too many reactive dependencies** – large computed properties with many dependencies can cause cascading updates.
- **Expensive watchers** – watchers that run heavy logic.
- **Unnecessary component updates** – components that re‑render even when props haven't changed (use `v-once`, `v-memo` in Vue 3.2+).
- **Large list rendering** – use virtual scrolling.
- **Third‑party libraries** – check if they cause performance issues.

quizData.question: Which tool can show you a flame graph of Vue component render times?
quizData.explanation: Vue Devtools has a Performance tab that records and displays component render timings.
